This surface integral can be written as a repeated integral, as shown below. 

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{2}\boxed{}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ defined by $z=g(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f(x,y,z)$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

For the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}(-\sqrt{2}x-y)=-\sqrt{2},
$$

and

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂y}=\frac{∂}{∂y}(-\sqrt{2}x-y)=-1.
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(-\sqrt{2})}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\sqrt{2}y\cdot 2\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{2}\,2\sqrt{2}y\,\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-1a33e921-a9bc-5edf-9d0c-b149f91622e1"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-1a33e921-a9bc-5edf-9d0c-b149f91622e1" :answer-field/id #uuid "1a33e921-a9bc-5edf-9d0c-b149f91622e1" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-abd564cc-a7f0-5f60-a224-edcb8733b99b" :answer-field/choices ["answer-246b6bfe-20aa-55cc-b239-3304de81494f" "answer-a9391385-1fbe-53da-993e-c0f38007e6e4" "answer-abd564cc-a7f0-5f60-a224-edcb8733b99b" "answer-72fa2757-f8e2-52c7-97eb-f3ea64fd0de1" "answer-fa49e0e8-2a63-57cc-8df5-3f02f87ef7e4"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-246b6bfe-20aa-55cc-b239-3304de81494f" :answer/id #uuid "246b6bfe-20aa-55cc-b239-3304de81494f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-2\sqrt{2}y" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a9391385-1fbe-53da-993e-c0f38007e6e4" :answer/id #uuid "a9391385-1fbe-53da-993e-c0f38007e6e4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-4\sqrt{2}{y}^{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-abd564cc-a7f0-5f60-a224-edcb8733b99b" :answer/id #uuid "abd564cc-a7f0-5f60-a224-edcb8733b99b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\sqrt{2}y" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-72fa2757-f8e2-52c7-97eb-f3ea64fd0de1" :answer/id #uuid "72fa2757-f8e2-52c7-97eb-f3ea64fd0de1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4\sqrt{2}y" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-fa49e0e8-2a63-57cc-8df5-3f02f87ef7e4" :answer/id #uuid "fa49e0e8-2a63-57cc-8df5-3f02f87ef7e4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{2}y" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186106060 :question/problem "Consider the surface integral of the function $f(x,y,z)=2xy,$ where the surface $S$ is defined by $z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ for $-1\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 2.$

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.

For the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}(3x-4y)=3,
$$

and

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂y}=\frac{∂}{∂y}(3x-4y)=-4.
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be evaluated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}(24xy+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(24xy+(3x-4y)^{2})\sqrt{1+{3}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{26}{∬}_{D}\,(24xy+9{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}-24xy)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{26}{∬}_{D}\,(9{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{26}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(9{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{26}{\int }_{1}^{2}{[9{x}^{2}y+\frac{16}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{26}{\int }_{1}^{2}(9{x}^{2}+\frac{16}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{26}{[3{x}^{3}+\frac{16}{3}x]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\sqrt{26}(24+\frac{32}{3}-3-\frac{16}{3}) \\  & =\frac{79}{3}\sqrt{26}\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-0d471815-2895-5fb8-bed5-64d74c7a07a5"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-0d471815-2895-5fb8-bed5-64d74c7a07a5" :answer-field/id #uuid "0d471815-2895-5fb8-bed5-64d74c7a07a5" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-b2c0bc18-5385-5a20-91df-0c00a7144747" :answer-field/choices ["answer-20eaebd4-47b4-5a06-b816-cc531888309e" "answer-ae2d7ec7-e4c0-578d-84f7-8e6cf8e46b7a" "answer-3829b03c-0d7f-5b85-969e-c475546e2d9f" "answer-6a510a5b-13c1-5f24-b8c2-ff019d89d2c0" "answer-b2c0bc18-5385-5a20-91df-0c00a7144747"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-20eaebd4-47b4-5a06-b816-cc531888309e" :answer/id #uuid "20eaebd4-47b4-5a06-b816-cc531888309e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{121}{3}\sqrt{26}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ae2d7ec7-e4c0-578d-84f7-8e6cf8e46b7a" :answer/id #uuid "ae2d7ec7-e4c0-578d-84f7-8e6cf8e46b7a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{25}{3}\sqrt{26}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3829b03c-0d7f-5b85-969e-c475546e2d9f" :answer/id #uuid "3829b03c-0d7f-5b85-969e-c475546e2d9f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{395}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6a510a5b-13c1-5f24-b8c2-ff019d89d2c0" :answer/id #uuid "6a510a5b-13c1-5f24-b8c2-ff019d89d2c0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{5}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b2c0bc18-5385-5a20-91df-0c00a7144747" :answer/id #uuid "b2c0bc18-5385-5a20-91df-0c00a7144747" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{79}{3}\sqrt{26}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-44573c5a-fe32-5ee3-9d3f-c65bffe1a9fd" :question/id #uuid "44573c5a-fe32-5ee3-9d3f-c65bffe1a9fd" :question/math-academy-id "q-161342" :question/problem "Evaluate the surface integral

where $S$ is defined by $z=x$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2}.$" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ defined by $z=g(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f(x,y,z)$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

For the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}(x)=1,
$$

and

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂y}=\frac{∂}{∂y}(x)=0.
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be evaluated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}2z\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\sqrt{1+{1}^{2}+(0)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{2}{∬}_{D}\,2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}[-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{y=0}^{y=\pi /2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}-2x(0-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{2}{[{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-867991c0-ff4c-568a-b34d-41463d47a5c5"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-867991c0-ff4c-568a-b34d-41463d47a5c5" :answer-field/id #uuid "867991c0-ff4c-568a-b34d-41463d47a5c5" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-137ced3c-e27e-55d0-a129-d7f6d14ddfc4" :answer-field/choices ["answer-6354a1eb-c050-5050-93ac-b70e93b7b31d" "answer-24d68779-dfc9-5e3b-9438-879f14f3462b" "answer-ba006680-3290-5c38-89b3-8d6c40bc62cd" "answer-1dee489f-a3c9-5e67-9010-8a2bb6344bd1" "answer-137ced3c-e27e-55d0-a129-d7f6d14ddfc4"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6354a1eb-c050-5050-93ac-b70e93b7b31d" :answer/id #uuid "6354a1eb-c050-5050-93ac-b70e93b7b31d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-24d68779-dfc9-5e3b-9438-879f14f3462b" :answer/id #uuid "24d68779-dfc9-5e3b-9438-879f14f3462b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ba006680-3290-5c38-89b3-8d6c40bc62cd" :answer/id #uuid "ba006680-3290-5c38-89b3-8d6c40bc62cd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1dee489f-a3c9-5e67-9010-8a2bb6344bd1" :answer/id #uuid "1dee489f-a3c9-5e67-9010-8a2bb6344bd1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\sqrt{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-137ced3c-e27e-55d0-a129-d7f6d14ddfc4" :answer/id #uuid "137ced3c-e27e-55d0-a129-d7f6d14ddfc4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-ac50dc50-55cb-5157-8205-32f49dbad931" :question/id #uuid "ac50dc50-55cb-5157-8205-32f49dbad931" :question/math-academy-id "q-161338" :question/problem "![](images/fe/fe04241f55bae9dae231be6486a3c53985c8dc4af9e9656787267d9d852f829e.png)

where $S$ is defined by $z=4x+\sqrt{3}y$ and whose domain is the circle of radius $1$ centered at $O,$ as shown above." :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ defined by $z=g(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f(x,y,z)$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

For the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}(4x+\sqrt{3}y)=4,
$$

and

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂y}=\frac{∂}{∂y}(4x+\sqrt{3}y)=\sqrt{3}.
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}(1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot \sqrt{1+{4}^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot \sqrt{20}\,\text{d}A \\  & =2\sqrt{5}{∬}_{D}\,(1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ our domain can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 1,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi }.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula for polar coordinates, where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we obtain

$$

$$

$$

\iint\limits_D f\left(x,y,g(x,y)\right) \sqrt{1+\left(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y}\right)^2} \: \text{d}A.
$$

For the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(1+x+y^2\right) = 1,
$$

and

$$
\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y} = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(1+x+y^2\right) = 2y.
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be evaluated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\frac{1}{\sqrt{z-x+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{(1+x+{y}^{2})-x+{y}^{2}}}\cdot \sqrt{1+{1}^{2}+(2y)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+2{y}^{2}}}\cdot \sqrt{2+4{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+2{y}^{2}}}\cdot \sqrt{2(1+2{y}^{2})}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+2{y}^{2}}}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{1+2{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\frac{1}{\cancel{\sqrt{1+2{y}^{2}}}}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot \cancel{\sqrt{1+2{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{2}{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot (1-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot 1\cdot 2 \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}

and

$$
\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y} = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(\sqrt2x-y) = -1.

$$

\iint\limits_S f(x,y,z) \, \textrm{d}S 
=
\iint\limits_D f(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \left\|  \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \right\|  \text{d}A.

Now, if a surface is given by the explicit equation $z=g(x,y)$ over a plane region $D$ in Cartesian coordinates, then the canonical parametrization of this surface is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,y) = \langle x,\:  y, \: g(x,y) \rangle, \qquad (x,y) \in D.
$$

$$

$$

$$
\iint\limits_S f(x,y,z) \, \textrm{d}S 
=
\iint\limits_D f\left(x,y,g(x,y)\right) \sqrt{1+\left(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y}\right)^2} \: \text{d}A.

These techniques allow physicists to compute quantities such as mass distributions, charge densities, and gravitational or electric potentials.

Concepts such as circulation, flux, and path independence lead to the fundamental theorems of vector calculus, including Green’s theorem, the divergence theorem, and Stokes’ theorem. Applications of multivariable calculus follow, including vector mechanics and optimization.
